newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Ariston says monitoring Cambodia closely.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Ariston says monitoring Cambodia closely.

text.p: Ariston Group of Companies of Malaysia said on Monday it is monitoring "the political development in Phnom Penh very closely", and that it will not "take any risks".

The property developer, Cambodia's largest single investor, did not elaborate on its comment in a statement released on Monday. But it said all of its 470 foreign employees in Cambodia are safe, and that its 400 local Cambodian employees have returned to their homes.

Bitter fighting between forces aligned with Cambodia's prime minister has shut down businesses in the capital city of Phnom Penh. Southeast Asian airlines suspended their flights to and from the city on Sunday.
At least 12 people were killed and 50 wounded in the weekend's fighting on the streets of the capital.
Ariston is involved in a $1.3 billion Sihanoukville project involving the redevelopments of the Kang Keng airport, as well as construction of a casino ahd hotel resort on Naga Island.
Malaysia is Cambodia's largest foreign investor, with over $3 billion. At least a dozen Malaysian companies have invested in projects in the country since 1994.

Other Malaysian companies also said they were tracking the situation at their Cambodian operations. Samling Corp Sdn Bhd, which has a logging concession covering 800,000 ha in western and southeastern Cambodia, said none of its businesses have been affected.

"Although, for the safety of our people, we've transferred most of the non-essential staff from Phnom Penh to the provinces," said Jeffrey Han, general manager in charge of the firm's Cambodia operations.
He said the firm has 1,400 employees in Cambodia, and remains "pretty committed to it (the country)". He also said his employees have reported that the fighting is contained.
An official at Malaysian national oil firm Petronas said all of the company's 12 petrol stations in Cambodia have stopped operations since Saturday.
He said his company's investments in Cambodia are "considered very small" compared to other firms', but declined to detail the size of the investment.
Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), Malaysia's top bank, said it has closed the bank's branch in Phnom Penh from Monday "until the situation returns to normal".
"We are in close contact with Malaysian Embassy in Phnom Penh for any further actions," said a Maybank spokesman.
